title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?
abstract: arXiv:2609.09038v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reasoning representations are increasingly used as explanations for large language model outputs. Yet they are typically evaluated with model-centric criteria, such as answer accuracy and faithfulness, leaving it unclear whether they help people evaluate model responses. In this work, we study reasoning representations as human-facing interfaces rather than proxies for model reasoning ability. We conduct a controlled human study of six reasoning formats across tasks of varying complexity, supported by a web-based framework that randomizes task domains, problem instances, and representation order. The study collects fine-grained judgments of structural understanding, error detection and localization, and trust calibration. Our study shows a mismatch between perceived preference and support for human evaluation. Participants prefer planning- and decomposition-based representations, but simpler chain-of-thought traces better support verific

translated_title: 推理表示是否有助于人类评估大语言模型的输出？
translated_abstract: 推理表示正被越来越多地用作大语言模型输出的解释。然而，它们通常以模型为中心的标准进行评估，例如答案准确性和忠实度，这使得它们是否能帮助人们评估模型响应仍不清楚。在这项工作中，我们将推理表示作为面向人类的交互界面进行研究，而不是作为模型推理能力的代理指标。我们开展了一项受控人类实验研究，涵盖六种推理格式在不同复杂程度任务中的表现，并由一个基于网络的框架提供支持，该框架对任务领域、问题实例和表示顺序进行随机化。该研究收集了关于结构理解、错误检测与定位以及信任校准的细粒度判断。我们的研究揭示了感知偏好与对人类评估实际支持之间的不匹配：参与者更偏好基于规划和分解的推理表示，但更简单的思维链轨迹反而能更好地支持验证。
tldr: 研究发现，尽管人们更偏好基于规划和分解的复杂推理表示，但更简单的思维链表示反而更能有效支持人类对大语言模型输出的评估。
en_tdlr: Although humans prefer planning- and decomposition-based reasoning representations, simpler chain-of-thought traces better support human evaluation of LLM outputs.
